draftArchitecture.plainAnswer: A fifteen-year sentence in a case involving AI-generated abuse does not itself remove images from the internet.
causalSequence: A fabricated image depicts an identifiable person in an intimate situation.
Publishing it without consent can expose that person to real harassment even though the event was invented.
A criminal prosecution addresses the offender; a platform-removal request addresses the hosted image.
draftArchitecture.workedCase: A friend finds a fake intimate image of herself on a covered platform and uses its removal process.
draftArchitecture.transferCase: If the platform ignores the valid request, reporting its failure to FTC differs from reporting the perpetrator to police.
draftArchitecture.usefulAction: Open the FTC guide for a valid platform request and the appropriate next reporting route; do not treat a conviction as automatic erasure.
draftArchitecture.formatSpecificStructure: The Story; LAiDIES Read; What This Means for You; Cocktail Party; source-linked Class Notes.
draftArchitecture.antiTemplateDecision: One news event followed by the distinction the reader actually needs; no generic AI productivity exercise.
